Sign Up




Find Your Campus By Your Degree
 











5 reasons to attend KSU’s Open House



Experience the Campus "Fit"
You can’t judge a college’s atmosphere by reading a brochure or looking at a website. You have to visit in person. Walk the campus and see the facilities. Many current students said they decided to apply because Kennesaw State just “felt” right.
Check out Housing
Explore your housing options — an in-person visit makes planning what to bring to your future home a whole lot easier. You’ll also see how living on campus provides easy access to resources, activities and events.
Delicious Food!
Enjoy a complimentary lunch in our award-winning dining facilities provided for up
                                       to three visitors.
Explore Scholarships and Aid
Figuring out financial aid can be a challenge. At Open House, financial aid counselors
                                       will answer questions and help you understand the types of aid, grants and scholarships
                                       available. Come learn about FAFSA, HOPE, student work and much more.
Learn about Majors and Programs
You can pick from academic sessions based on KSU’s colleges. You will get a feel for what KSU courses and faculty are like, and you can ask questions about degrees or academic opportunities.









Visit our Campus!

Visiting campus is a great opportunity to explore KSU and learn about Owl Nation.
Kennesaw State is a student-centered, research-driven university with a vibrant campus
                           culture and an entrepreneurial spirit. As Owls, we are guided by a purpose and, no
                           matter how we change, grow, or evolve, we never forget who we are. Welcome to Owl
                           Nation!

Know More, Borrow Less




In the Fall of 2018, University System of Georgia Chancellor, Steve Wrigley, launched an initiative to ensure students are aware of their student loan debt. The Know More, Borrow Less (KMBL) initiative supports the USG’s three primary objectives: graduate more students, be more affordable and be more efficient. This initiative is designed to reduce barriers to aid, improve students’ understanding of borrowing and reduce student debt.
To support this initiative, a “debt letter” will be electronically sent in a mobile-friendly format to every enrolled student who currently has student loan debt resulting from federal or state loan programs, or private lender borrowing. Students will receive both a text and an email providing them a link to a personalized letter containing specific information on monthly payments based on their current loan amounts. Each academic year, students will receive a debt letter, updating them on their cumulative student loan debt. The Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid will have analytics to review the open rate of these messages to ensure students are receiving the information.

Engineering student uses NASA data to study distant star systems


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 7, 2026

Thi Tran
Kennesaw State University electrical engineering student Thi Tran never imagined herself conducting astronomy research. Now, she is
                     using data from a NASA satellite to help researchers distinguish distant planets from
                     stars that can produce nearly identical signals.
Tran, who is originally from Vietnam, is studying observations from NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, or TESS. The satellite monitors stars and looks for repeated dips in brightness that may occur when a planet passes in front of one.
“When an object goes in front of the star, it blocks a little bit of the light and causes a dip in the brightness that we observe,” Tran said. “If that dip repeats over and over, there might be a planet orbiting that star.”
The challenge is that binary star systems can produce similar signals. When two stars orbit one another and one passes in front of the other, the change in brightness can resemble the pattern created by a planet. Tran’s research focuses on determining which type of system researchers are observing.
Making that distinction can save astronomers valuable telescope time while also providing useful information about binary stars. Researchers can study those systems to estimate characteristics such as the stars’ masses and sizes.
“By understanding other stars, we will know more about the sun, and where it is in its lifetime or what we expect to happen when it evolves,” Tran said.
Tran moved to the United States in 2020 and studied English and mathematics at Gwinnett
                     Technical College before professors encouraged her to pursue electrical engineering.
                     She transferred to Kennesaw State in 2024 and enrolled in the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology.
Although the project centers on astronomy, Tran said it connects closely to her electrical engineering studies. She analyzes light curves and graphs showing how a star’s brightness changes over time and looks for repeating patterns using skills similar to signal processing in her major.
Research, however, was initially unfamiliar territory.
“At first, I didn’t think that I was capable of doing research at all,” Tran said. “But now, after two semesters, I get the idea that research is a learning process. It’s not about solving the problem at first sight.”
One of the project’s biggest lessons came after Tran and her research team spent months analyzing a star system that produced confusing results. Their model suggested characteristics that did not make sense together, prompting them to investigate further.
They eventually discovered that the signal they were studying was coming from a different
                     star than they initially believed.
“The challenge of this research is that we don’t know the answer,” Tran said. “Even if there are published papers talking about it already, we still have to study it further.”
Tran credits Associate Professor of Physics David Joffe with encouraging her to pursue research and helping her work through
                     difficult questions.
“Thi has shown tremendous curiosity, persistence and a willingness to work through difficult problems,” Joffe said. “She has grown tremendously as a researcher, and her ability to bring her engineering background into this project has made her an important part of our work.”
Tran has submitted a manuscript based on the research to a journal and is awaiting
                     review. She said the project has opened her eyes to opportunities she had not previously
                     considered.
“A year ago, I didn’t know anything about research or the opportunities KSU could bring,” Tran said. “Now I know research is a learning process, and I’m excited to see where it can take me.”
– Story by Raynard Churchwell

Executive MBA Alumna Named an Atlanta Woman of Influence






Executive MBA Alumna Named an Atlanta Woman of Influence


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 6, 2026

Kennesaw State University alumna Carmen Chubb, president of Columbia Residential,
                     former Chief of Staff to the Mayor of Atlanta, and a powerful advocate for affordable
                     housing, has been named a 2026 Woman of Influence by the Atlanta Business Chronicle.
Chubb, who earned her Executive MBA from KSU’s Michael J. Coles College of Business in 2020, will be recognized by ABC at a ceremony on Oct. 8 at the Stave Room in Atlanta. The Women of Influence awards honor women who have made significant strides in their careers and are making a difference in their organizations and communities.
Having experienced housing insecurity as a child, Chubb has made it her life’s mission to help people find affordable homes.
“Making sure families have housing they can afford is important to me because my parents divorced when I was young, and my family was housing insecure,” Chubb said. “We had a home, but it was a struggle to afford it, and we lived with the stress of that insecurity for many years.”
Chubb learned the ins and outs of the housing industry by working for a bank’s mortgage department before taking a job with the Georgia Housing and Finance Authority (later renamed the Georgia Department of Community Affairs), where she spent 23 years administering federal and state affordable housing programs.
She left the GDCA in 2019 to become Chief of Staff to Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms, where she oversaw critical city operations and served as the mayor’s top advisor. In 2022, Chubb joined Columbia Residential as president. Columbia Residential is a real estate developer that partners with governments and community organizations to build affordable housing in Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Tennessee, and Florida.
As her career continued to evolve, Chubb joined the KSU Executive MBA program in 2018 to enhance her leadership skills and to prepare for the next challenge. She graduated while still working for the Mayor’s Office.
Designed for experienced working professionals, Kennesaw State's Executive MBA program
                     combines once-a-month weekend residencies, collaborative team experiences, international
                     study, and individualized executive coaching throughout the program to help students
                     sharpen their business acumen and grow into strategic leaders.
“My EMBA honed my business and finance skills and positioned me to transition from the public sector to the private sector,” she said. “The finance and economics coursework – not to mention the leadership focus and team setting – challenged me and prepared me for the role I have now as president of Columbia Residential.”
Richard James, KSU’s Executive Director of MBA Programs, said Chubb’s recognition as an Atlanta Business Chronicle Woman of Influence reflects the leadership qualities she demonstrated as a student in the program.
“Carmen embodies all the qualities that we hope to see from the alumni of our EMBA program,” James said. “She is a powerful leader with a keen understanding of business and a genuine desire to serve others. She has become a role model for our EMBA students.”
In addition to her professional achievements, Chubb has also made building up others
                     a part of her personal mission. She regularly mentors young colleagues at Columbia
                     Residential; she sits on the boards of the KSU Foundation, Open Doors Atlanta, and
                     Community ImPACT; and volunteers with Back On My Feet Atlanta, an organization that
                     uses running to promote accountability, social engagement, resilience, and physical
                     fitness.
As Chubb prepares to accept the Woman of Influence Award, she is grateful that her
                     career has provided her with countless opportunities to relate to and learn from people
                     of all walks of life.
“These connections have made me a better human,” she said, “and that better human shows up in all spaces that I enter: my home, my work, and in my service.”
-Patrick Harbin

Kennesaw State names nursing simulation lab in honor of Katherine Scott






Kennesaw State names nursing simulation lab in honor of Katherine Scott


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 6, 2026
$1 million gift establishes enduring scholarship support for future nurses

Katherine A. Scott and Lance Burchett
Kennesaw State University has honored longtime donor Katherine A. Scott by naming
                     a nursing simulation lab in recognition of her $1 million gift establishing the Katherine
                     A. Scott Nursing Scholarship Endowment.
The Katherine Scott Simulation Lab was formally dedicated during a Sept. 9 celebration
                     at the Wellstar School of Nursing. The space provides nursing students with opportunities to develop clinical skills
                     through hands-on simulation and practice.
“Katherine’s generosity reminds us that philanthropy is more than financial giving. It is about expressing confidence in the next generation and creating opportunities for hard-working students to thrive and launch meaningful careers,” said Ivan Pulinkala, provost and executive vice president for academic affairs.
The endowment will provide enduring scholarship support for nursing students, helping reduce financial barriers as they prepare for careers in one of the nation’s most vital health care professions. More than 1,000 students are pursuing nursing education at Kennesaw State.
“Kennesaw State University has a very unique and compelling student body,” said Lance Burchett, vice president for advancement and CEO of the KSU Foundation. “Approximately 40% of our students are Pell Grant-eligible, and another 40% are seeking to become the first in their family to earn a college degree. While 79% of our students qualify for financial aid, only 6% receive donor-funded scholarships. Those students are 80% more likely to graduate in four years. They tell us it’s because of the gravity of having someone believe in them — the realization that ‘someone is investing in me, and I don’t want to let them down.’”
For Scott, the decision to support nursing students is rooted in a lifelong connection to health care. At 8 years old, she became seriously ill with undulant fever and experienced firsthand the impact of being cared for. Her early interest in medicine continued throughout childhood, when she played doctor with orange crates and carried a small black doctor’s bag.

Although her parents did not encourage her to attend college, Scott ultimately became an X-ray technician and found a career she loved. Her experiences shaped a lasting belief in the importance of following one’s passion and making a difference in others’ lives.
“I am giving, and these students are receiving the opportunity to learn, grow, and prepare for their careers,” Scott said. “What they receive here will carry over to the patients they care for. That is what giving and receiving means to me, and I hope these students remember their purpose, approach nursing with passion, and keep their focus on healing and caring for others.”
Scott’s commitment to Kennesaw State extends beyond nursing. In 2017, she established the Katherine Scott Rehearsal Hall Endowment with a $500,000 gift supporting the Dr. Bobbie Bailey School of Music. The rehearsal hall inside the Dr. Bobbie Bailey and Family Performance Center bears
                     her name and supports music education and performance opportunities.
“These labs provide students with an invaluable opportunity to practice scenarios and techniques, develop advanced skills in teamwork and time management, and learn to balance the care of multiple patients and competing priorities in a safe, supportive environment,” said Laurie Tis, interim dean of the Wellstar College of Health and Human Services.
The naming celebration also brought Scott together with nursing students who shared
                     their experiences and aspirations as future health care professionals.
“Your generosity is not simply providing us with a space to learn. You are helping us become the health care professionals we aspire to be,” said Violet Miller, a student in the Wellstar School of Nursing.
Through the Katherine A. Scott Nursing Scholarship Endowment and the newly named simulation lab, Scott’s generosity will have a lasting impact, helping future nurses pursue their education, develop their skills, and carry that investment forward to the patients and communities they serve.

Engineering student combines technical and marketing skills through hands-on experiences


                        						KENNESAW, Ga. | 
                        						Oct 5, 2026

Cynthia Konziase
Kennesaw State University student Cynthia Konziase is building a versatile skill set
                     by combining industrial and systems engineering with marketing and hands-on industry
                     experience through opportunities within the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology (SPCEET).
From serving as a marketing student assistant in the dean’s office to completing an internship with Vantage Industries, the Lawrenceville native has gained firsthand experience in communication, project coordination, and operational problem-solving. Those experiences built on a foundation that began long before college, rooted in an early interest in engineering and a desire to blend technical and business-minded thinking.
Konziase said that Kennesaw State stood out to her because of the opportunities available
                     on the Marietta Campus. She would later decide to major in Industrial Engineering Technology, which proved to be a natural fit because it allowed Konziase to combine her technical
                     interests with strengths she had already developed in business and marketing.
“I knew I wanted to go into engineering, but I also knew that my strong suits were in business and marketing,” she said. “Industrial engineering combines a lot of those concepts.”
That blend of interests has shaped the experiences Konziase has pursued outside the
                     classroom.
As a marketing student assistant in the SPCEET dean’s office, she has gained experience supporting communications and marketing efforts while developing skills that complement her engineering coursework. At the same time, her internship with Vantage Industries, an Atlanta-based performance textiles manufacturer, has allowed her to apply industrial engineering
                     concepts in a hands-on professional environment.
“Cynthia’s experience is a great example of how our students can take what they learn in the classroom and apply it across different areas,” SPCEET Interim Dean Christina Scherrer said. “By developing technical expertise alongside communication, business, and real-world problem-solving skills, she is preparing herself to contribute in a variety of professional environments.”
Konziase discovered the Vantage Industries internship through KSU Director of Industry
                     and STEM Partnerships Kent Lusk, who knew she was seeking hands-on experience. Lusk
                     connected her with the company after learning it needed help addressing operational
                     challenges.
Her work has focused on improving operations within a section of the company’s warehouse, requiring her to take on responsibilities that change from day to day. Some days involve identifying goals for the space and coordinating with employees as machinery or pallets are moved. Other assignments require her to log products, organize information in spreadsheets, or communicate with outside companies.
The experience has allowed Konziase to see how industrial and systems engineering
                     extends beyond calculations and technical design. The field also requires communication,
                     organization, project coordination, and an understanding of how people and processes
                     interact.
“There are many nuances to this warehouse space optimization project that require a lot of detail and attention, and things that I may not be able to experience everywhere,” Konziase said. “My manager at the time, Jason Fountain, was also a great help throughout the process and offered a lot of valuable advice.”
As she continues her studies at Kennesaw State, Konziase said the experiences have
                     helped her see how her different interests can work together in her future career.
“I’ve learned that I don’t have to limit myself to just one area,” Konziase said. “Engineering, business, and marketing all require problem-solving and working with people, and I want to continue finding ways to bring those skills together.”
– Story by Raynard Churchwell

Master’s in Fintech: Digital Payment Technologies




Earn a Master of Science in Digital Financial Technologies (Fintech) and build advanced
                              skills in digital payments, financial data analytics, and cybersecurity. The program
                              is flexible, 100% online, and designed for working professionals.
You’ll study modern payment experiences, including platforms like PayPal, Cash App, and Apple Pay. You’ll learn how secure transactions move through today’s financial systems.
Fintech is one of the fastest-growing areas in financial services, with strong demand for professionals who can combine technology and finance skills. You’ll be prepared for leadership roles in digital payments, financial data analytics, cybersecurity, and the technologies shaping the future of finance.
Kennesaw State University offers a distinctive program in digital payment technologies.
                              It combines payments expertise, analytics skills, and industry-aligned coursework
                              in a flexible online format.
Join an Upcoming Virtual Info Session
Learn more about the program, meet faculty, and get your questions answered.
Apply Now







Contact Us

Contact us to receive more information.

Thank you for interest in the Fintech Graduate Degree Program

 
By submitting your information, you consent to KSU using the information to contact
                                    you via phone, text message, or email for informational and promotional purposes.
                                    more To learn more about how KSU collects and processes personal data, read our Privacy and Legal Notice.













Is a Fintech Master’s Right for You?




This program may be a good fit if you: 

Work in financial services, technology, cybersecurity, data analytics, or operations
Want to change careers and move into fintech or the digital payments industry
Need an online, flexible master’s program designed for working professionals
Want to understand the systems, data, and innovations driving modern financial services
Are looking for a graduate degree with national and global career opportunities 




















Why Choose the KSU Master’s in Fintech?




Study in a Leading Global Fintech Hub: More than 70% of U.S. payment card transactions flow through companies based in Georgia, many of them in Metro Atlanta. You’ll learn in one of the most active regions for digital payments and financial technology.
100% Online and Built for Working Professionals: This fully online program is flexible and designed to fit alongside your career and
                                    personal commitments.
Industry-Aligned Curriculum Taught by Experts: Courses are taught by faculty with deep experience in payments and fintech. You’ll learn skills that are practical, current, and aligned with employer needs.
Master the Technologies Driving Fintech Growth: You’ll learn how digital payment systems work, how data supports decision-making, and how cybersecurity, risk, and compliance protect financial systems. 






















Program at a Glance


Format: 100% Online
Length: 30 credit hours
Structure: 21 core hours + 9 elective hours
Pace: Full-time or part-time
Start Dates: Fall and Spring
Designed For: Working professionals, career changers, and those looking to move into fintech 

See the full Curriculum





What You’ll Learn


Advanced digital payment systems
Machine learning in financial services
Financial data analytics and data pipelines
Cybersecurity, risk mitigation, and fraud prevention
Regulatory and compliance analysis for digital payments
Technology integration across financial systems
Business intelligence and data-driven decision-making
Emerging fintech tools and technologies

These skills prepare you for roles across product, analytics, security, compliance,
                                    and technology.










Tuition, Financial Aid & Support

Kennesaw State offers competitive tuition and financial aid options for graduate students. Our advising team can help you understand costs, explore financial aid, and plan your next steps.







Fintech Careers and Job Opportunities

Graduates pursue roles across many areas of fintech, including:

Digital Payments Analyst
Fintech Product or Project Manager
Financial Data or Business Intelligence Analyst
Fraud, Risk, and Compliance Analyst
Cybersecurity Analyst (Financial Services)
Financial or Payments Systems Analyst
Business Analyst (Fintech or Financial Services)
Technology Operations or Integration Specialist 








Ready to Take the Next Step?




Request Information




Attend an Info Session




Start Your Application










See How KSU Is Shaping the Future of Fintech

KSU prepares students to advance their careers in digital payments, analytics, and
                           financial innovation. See how enrolling in can put you on the cutting edge of fintech.


Gain the skills and industry knowledge to stand out in one of the world’s fastest-growing areas of financial technology—all in a flexible, 100% online format designed for working professionals.







Stories of Transformation

Our students come from diverse backgrounds, including business, IT, design, and non-technical fields, and each found a unique path into fintech through KSU. Hear how the students and alumni have advanced their careers through fintech.



I realized I could do this, even if I was scared.







Our mind can be the biggest obstacle. Push past that point. You can reach goals you
                                                   never imagined.

Ananda Johnson







I created a fintech solution that helps the unbanked.







This class inspired me to develop CreditLift: an AI-powered alternative credit scoring
                                                   system.

Didier Lopez







I wanted a career change, and fintech finally made it click.







I wanted to combine finance and technology. And when I found the fintech program at
                                                      KSU, everything just made sense.

Ashley Harper

About KSU

Kennesaw State is a comprehensive university located on two suburban campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta, northwest of metro Atlanta. We are making an impact across the region, the nation and around the world. As the third largest university in Georgia, Kennesaw State has nearly 43,000 students enrolled in over 180 undergraduate, master’s, doctoral degree and certificate programs.

Using D2L Brightspace to Access Courses

 D2L Brightspace is Kennesaw State University’s learning management system for accessing course materials, assignments, updates, and support resources. Faculty and staff can find detailed guidance on course management, while students can access information on current and upcoming courses, including course date modifications and eCore resources.
Stay informed with updates shared in D2L announcements and system improvements communicated
                     through regular university updates!

Quick Links

Introduction to D2L Training for Instructors
D2L Information for Students
Introduction to D2L Video for Students
Search the KSU Knowledge Base

D2L Information for Faculty and Staff

Faculty and staff may find detailed information about course availability, course-related requests (course shell, course reset, third party integration, enrollment), account access, and updates to the D2L system and related technologies in the D2L Information for Faculty & Staff section.

Getting Started in D2L - Training Course for Instructors

Dive into the basics of using D2L at KSU, exploring key features like grades, quizzes,
                           and groups. Perfect for beginners, videos in this OwlTrain journey provide step-by-step
                           guidance to help you navigate and utilize D2L Brightspace effectively.
Get started with D2L Brightspace Basics for Instructors in OwlTrain and begin your learning journey today! 

Faculty: Course Availability Information






                                       Current Term and Immediately Upcoming Term
                                       



Courses that have been assigned to instructors in Owl Express will be available in
                                             D2L within 24 hours of being assigned in Owl Express once the initial course load
                                             for the term has occurred. The initial course load occurs approximately one month
                                             before the start of the term and is announced in D2L Announcements.
If courses for the term have been loaded and you do not see your course, please check
                                             with your department to be sure you are the instructor of record in Owl Express.






Future Term Courses - Instructor access



Owl Express (Banner) courses are available to instructors in D2L approximately one month prior to the start of the term. 
If earlier access is needed for course-building, instructors may request a course
                                             shell using the Course Shell Request Form. Content can be copied into the Banner course once available. Refer to the Knowledge
                                             Base article How to Copy Course Components in D2L for Instructors for instructions.
Note for new faculty:  Accounts are created in D2L at the same time that courses are loaded, so you will not be able to log in to D2L until approximately one month prior to the start of term. If earlier access is required, you must complete a manual account request (more information in the D2L Account information section of this page). 






Student Access to Current and Past Terms 



Student access to D2L courses begins on the published course start date and ends 60 days after the course end date, unless modified by the instructor.
Instructors may grant early or extended access by editing the course’s start and/or end dates. Refer to the KSU Knowledge Base article How to Change a Course’s Start and End Dates in D2L for step‑by‑step instructions. Please note especially the start dates for later parts of term.
For additional assistance, visit the KSU Service Portal or email the Service Desk at service@kennesaw.edu. 







Additional Instructor Information





Course Content - Related Information



Course Shell Requests
Please use the Course Shell Request Form to request a non-Owl Express (non-credit) course for D2L Brightspace. To request an Owl Express course, please email the Registrar’s Office at registrar@kennesaw.edu. 
A course shell functions identically to a normal course, but has no start or end date,
                                             and no automated student enrollment functionality. The course instructor must handle
                                             participant enrollment. Course shells cannot be used for course credit-earning activities.
Course Reset Requests
In the case of content errors, UITS Learning Technologies administrators can perform
                                             a D2L course reset upon request. Course Reset will return the course back to an empty
                                             shell in a single, permanent action. This process purges all data and there is no
                                             restore. A key feature is that it will not affect user enrollments. To reduce the
                                             chance of unintentional deletions, the instructor of record must complete and submit
                                             the Course Reset Request Form.
Third-party Integration Requests for D2L Brightspace
Many third-party publishers and vendors offer integrations with the ability to connect
                                             to D2L Brightspace courses. University Information Technology Services (UITS) and
                                             Digital Learning Innovations (DLI) facilitate and support these integrations but require
                                             advance notice (one semester preferred) to ensure both successful implementation and
                                             compliance to university accessibility and quality requirements. All third-party integrations
                                             must be reviewed and approved before implementation.
Refer to the KSU Knowledge Base article How to Check for Existing Third-Party Tools in D2L to confirm whether the tool is already available in D2L Brightspace.
If the tool name does not appear in the Existing Activities or External Learning Tools
                                             lists, begin the request process by following the steps outlined in the D2L Third-Party Integration Request Process article.






D2L Account Information



Assignment to an Owl Express course will result in the automatic creation of the user’s account. Please allow 48 hours after instructor assignment or student registration for the account to appear.
If there will be no assignment in Owl Express, please use the D2L Manual User Account Creation form to request an account. Please see notes based on account type.
For Student AccountsIf the student account does not have a @students.kennesaw.edu email address, please
                                             email Service Desk at service@kennesaw.edu to request an email override before completing the D2L account request. 
For Faculty/Staff AccountsFaculty and staff must have a Buckley form with a current FERPA certificate on file
                                             with the Office of the Registrar before we can create a D2L account. FERPA training
                                             occurs in October each year or within 30 days of hiring, so a current certificate
                                             will be from your most recent assignment of FERPA training. We must verify this with
                                             the Office of the Registrar and the process can take a couple of days. We appreciate
                                             your patience. We cannot accept forms directly from faculty/staff.
If you know that these requirements have not yet been met and would like to get the
                                             process started, please see the following information:
1.  Please complete FERPA training found on OwlTrain.
You will need to login to the OwlTrain system using your KSU credentials. You can find the FERPA training assignment under Compliance (click the square icon with nine dots in the top left of the home page) or under My Assignments on the home page. Please save a PDF of your FERPA certificate as you will need to upload it to the Buckley form.  Refer to How to Download and Print Your Completion Certificate  to locate your certificate in OwlTrain. 
Important: If you do not see FERPA training, please check to see if you have a certificate dated
                                             October or newer. If you do, your training is current and you may attach that certificate
                                             to your Buckley form. If you have no certificate or your certificate dates from before
                                             October, please email service@kennesaw.edu to request that the FERPA training be added to your account. If your start date is in the future, please ask your supervisor to request the training on your behalf. 
2.  Please complete the Buckley form found on the Banner Security Forms page, and please note:

Be sure to complete all indicated fields and click the FINISH button.
Make sure your supervisor is expecting to sign the form as the links are time-sensitive.







Course Enrollment - Related Information



Manual Enrollment of Instructor(s) to D2L Course (emergency)
Manual enrollment into a course should be performed by the instructor of the course
                                             whenever possible. How to Add Participants to a D2L Course provides instructions for enrolling participants in a course. 
Enrollment by UITS of faculty or staff into an Owl Express course where the person
                                             is not the instructor of record will require the permission of the department chair
                                             or dean. The Manual Enrollment of Instructor(s) to D2L Course form may be used by a department chair to request enrollment of self and/or other instructors. A delegate of the chair may complete the form but must attach a PDF of an email showing the chair's permission for the requested enrollment. 
Enroll 20+ Participants to D2L Course Shell
Enrollment of fewer than 20 participants into a non-Owl Express course should be handled
                                             by the instructor of the course. How to Add Participants to a D2L Course provides instructions for enrolling participants in a course. 
You may use the Enroll 20+ Participants form to request assistance with bulk enrollment when you have 20 or more participants to
                                             enroll into a non-Owl Express (non-credit) course shell.

D2L News for Students

Students may find detailed information about course availability, eCore/GoVIEW courses, D2L notifications, and updates to the D2L interface and functionality in the D2L Information for Students section. 

Getting Started in D2L for Students

Refer to the OwlTrain video Getting Started with D2L for Students to learn more about KSU's online learning platform, D2L Brightspace.

When can I see my courses in D2L? 





Access to Previous Term Courses



Courses will be visible to students in D2L until 60 days past the published end date of the course unless the end date has been adjusted by the instructor. 
If you can no longer access a KSU D2L course because the end date of the course has
                                             passed and you need access to the course, please reach out to the instructor of the
                                             course. If the instructor is not reachable, please reach out to the department where
                                             the course was offered.






Access to Future Term Courses



New Students
New students registered for an upcoming term will not have an account in D2L until
                                             courses for the upcoming term are loaded into D2L, approximately one month before
                                             the start of term. Once your account is created, you may log in, but you will not
                                             see your registered courses until the published start date of the course unless the
                                             start date has been adjusted by the instructor.
All Students
You will not see your registered courses in D2L until the published start date of
                                             the course unless the start date has been adjusted by the instructor. Start dates
                                             vary based on part of term. These dates may be found by visiting the Academic Calendars web page and navigating to the upcoming term. 






Finding eCore Courses



Your eCore courses will not be found in the KSU D2L Brightspace. Georgia Online Virtual Instruction Enterprise Wide (GoVIEW) is where you can access USG eCore courses. 
For technical assistance, visit the KSU eCore contact page. The KSU service desk will not be able to assist with login to eCore. 
To learn more about eCore courses, visit the KSU eCore home page.

Who We Are




We’re UITS! We are the technology division at Kennesaw State University working behind the scenes to support all Owls by ensuring you have seamless access to technology. Whether you’re logging in with your NetID, confirming your identity with Microsoft Authenticator, navigating your courses on D2L, sending emails through KSUmail, or collaborating on Teams while connected to KSU Wi-Fi, UITS is here to support every step of your tech journey.
Learn more about UITS
 
KSU’s Chief Information Officer (CIO), Aaron Streimish, oversees the strategic direction of our department and ensures that our technology initiatives align with the goals of KSU. He is a strong advocate for leveraging technology to enhance the learning experience, streamline operations and foster a collaborative campus community. Under his leadership, our division is dedicated to providing the services to support all Owls to achieve academic excellence, innovative research, and be able to collaborate across divisions and departments. 
Learn more about Our CIO
 
The Information Technology Advisory Committee (ITAC) at Kennesaw State University serves as a collaborative forum that connects academic, administrative, and technical perspectives to guide the university’s strategic direction in information technology. The committee advises on policies, priorities, and initiatives that enhance the effectiveness, security, and innovation of KSU’s technology environment.
